_meta: Keys distributed across a set of server nodes (for a cache or a sharded store), and what happens when a node is ADDED. Two placement schemes are compared. Modulo hashing assigns key -> node index (hash % N); it is simple but when N changes -- one node added or removed -- almost every key's (hash % N) changes, so almost every key moves to a different node (a mass cache miss / data reshuffle). Consistent hashing places both the nodes and the keys on a ring (positions 0..99 here) and sends each key to the first node clockwise; adding a node only steals the keys in the arc just before it, so only about K/N keys move and they all go to the new node -- everything else stays put. To make the fractions exact and reproducible, each key carries an explicit ring position (`pos`) and an explicit `hash` value (both standing in for real hash outputs). nodes are the four existing nodes with their ring positions; new_node is the node being added. Every assignment and move count is computed.
